name: Sketches
title: Before the
first stitch.
intro: A sketch leaves room for possibility. Follow the lines, explore the proportions, and see how a first thought begins to take shape.
alt: Illustrative graphite fashion drawings in an open sketchbook.
note: Leave a little room for the unexpected.

details.label: Silhouette
details.title: Start with the outline.
details.text: The outer line gives a garment its first impression. Notice the long shapes and the space around the body.
details.prompt: Follow the line from shoulder to hem.

details.label: Movement
details.title: Let the marks move.
details.text: Loose, repeated pencil strokes suggest a fold, a turn, or the direction of falling cloth. The drawing can stay open to change.
details.prompt: Look for the diagonal sweeps of fabric.

details.label: Proportion
details.title: Change one relationship.
details.text: A higher waist or a longer skirt changes the balance of a look. Sketching makes it possible to compare ideas before committing to one.
details.prompt: Compare the upper and lower parts of each figure.

steps: Collect a shape, a gesture, or a small detail.
Draw variations without polishing every mark.
Choose the lines that give the idea its character.
closing: A collection can begin with a single line.

name: Mood boards
title: Gather a
feeling.
intro: An image, a colour, a fragment of texture. Bring them together and a visual direction begins to emerge.
alt: Illustrative mood board with architectural photographs, botanical stems, paper and fabric samples.

details.label: Shape
details.title: Find a common rhythm.
details.text: An arch, a draped sculpture, a curved edge. Repeated shapes can connect references that come from very different places.
details.prompt: Notice the arches and soft curves.

details.label: Palette
details.title: Let colours speak together.
details.text: Cream, oat, warm brown, and a muted rose create a quiet starting point. The palette below is an illustrative direction for this study.
details.prompt: Compare the lightest and darkest tones.

details.label: Texture
details.title: Look beyond the image.
details.text: Paper, woven cloth, and dry botanical shapes bring different surfaces into the same story. Their contrast can suggest details for a garment.
details.prompt: Look at the contrast between smooth paper and woven cloth.

steps: Follow references that share a feeling.
Find repeating colours, shapes, and surfaces.
Keep the references that make the direction clearer.
closing: Inspiration becomes a language of its own.

name: Fabric swatches
title: A feeling
for fabric.
intro: Before a material becomes a garment, there is the pleasure of looking closely. Explore four textures and imagine how each could change a silhouette.
alt: Illustrative overlapping fabric samples in ivory, cocoa, rose and sheer cream.
note: A small sample. A new direction.

details.label: Ivory weave
details.title: An open, tactile surface.
details.text: The visible weave and softly frayed edge give this sample a relaxed character. Its texture becomes part of the design.
details.prompt: Look at the tiny spaces between the threads.

details.label: Cocoa texture
details.title: Depth in a darker tone.
details.text: The dense, nubbled surface makes the cocoa sample feel substantial in the composition. It provides contrast beside lighter layers.
details.prompt: Notice how the surface catches small pockets of shadow.

details.label: Rose drape
details.title: Softness in the folds.
details.text: Gentle highlights follow the rose sample as it folds. That change between light and shadow helps describe its movement.
details.prompt: Trace the light along the edge of a fold.

details.label: Sheer layer
details.title: A little light passing through.
details.text: The pale translucent layer lets the tones beneath remain visible. Overlapping it changes both the colour and the sense of depth.
details.prompt: Compare a single layer with an overlapping fold.

steps: See how a sample falls and forms folds.
Explore a contrast or a quiet tonal combination.
closing: The material brings its own voice.

name: Pattern-making
title: From line
to form.
intro: The worktable is where a drawing becomes a construction idea. Explore the marks that connect a flat pattern to a three-dimensional shape.
alt: Illustrative kraft-paper garment patterns, a curved ruler, scissors and measuring tape.

details.label: Outline
details.title: Define the piece.
details.text: The outline describes the shape of a pattern piece. Curves and straight edges begin to explain how the garment will be assembled.
details.prompt: Follow the shoulder, armhole, and side edge.

details.label: Direction
details.title: Give the piece a direction.
details.text: A direction line helps communicate how a pattern sits on fabric. In this simplified diagram, the long arrow makes that orientation visible.
details.prompt: Compare the arrow with the long edge of the piece.

details.label: Shaping
details.title: Make room for form.
details.text: A shaping mark suggests how a flat surface can be brought closer to the body. This diagram is an exploration of form, not a cutting pattern.
details.prompt: Notice the triangular mark near the waist.

steps: Identify the pieces behind a silhouette.
Mark the lines that explain their relationships.
Check the idea in a sample before refining it.
closing: Precision gives an idea room to become real.

name: Fittings
title: A conversation
with form.
intro: Fitting is a moment to pause and observe. A small change can alter the balance, comfort, and expression of the whole silhouette.
alt: Illustrative hands pinning a cream toile on a dress form.

details.label: Balance
details.title: Read the whole silhouette.
details.text: Start with the overall relationship of shoulder, waist, and hem. Look for areas where the cloth rests naturally or appears to pull.
details.prompt: Observe the garment before focusing on a single seam.

details.label: Shape
details.title: Let a pin suggest the change.
details.text: Pinning holds a possible adjustment long enough to assess it. A temporary change can reveal a different line without making it final.
details.prompt: Look at the cloth gathering around the pinned area.

details.label: Revisit
details.title: Keep the conversation open.
details.text: An adjustment is a proposal. Looking again from another angle helps decide whether it supports the intention of the design.
details.prompt: Imagine the same form from the side and the back.

steps: Take in the overall shape before changing it.
Try one considered alteration at a time.
Return to the complete silhouette and assess it again.
closing: The smallest adjustment can change the whole feeling.

name: Photoshoot
title: Into
the frame.
intro: A finished look takes on another life in a photograph. Browse the contact sheet and explore how colour, pose, and setting tell different stories.
alt: Original photograph of a model in a navy and pale-blue dress holding a flowing sheer wrap.
handwritten: One look. A new point of view.
note: A gesture held in a frame.

details.label: Movement
details.title: Let the fabric lead.
details.text: The lifted wrap draws a wide shape around the model. Pale layers catch the light against the blue dress and the outdoor setting.
details.prompt: Follow the curve from one raised hand to the other.
details.credit: Photograph: Memory Mirage · Original supplied image.

details.label: Structure
details.title: A quieter, closer frame.
details.text: A restrained pose brings the curved dark piping of the mauve jacket forward. The simple backdrop lets those lines remain clear.
details.prompt: Trace the curved lines across the front of the jacket.
details.credit: Original photograph supplied for this portfolio.

details.label: Colour
details.title: Give the print its space.
details.text: The fabric is opened toward the camera so the vivid figures and botanical forms can be seen together. The pose becomes part of the presentation.
details.prompt: Notice how holding the cloth reveals more of the composition.
details.credit: Original photograph supplied for this portfolio.

steps: Choose what the image should draw attention to.
Look at the relationship between pose, cloth, and light.
Find the photograph that carries the story most clearly.
closing: A photograph holds the moment a garment comes alive.

name: Crafts
title: The human
touch.
intro: A stitch, a fold, a carefully placed bead. Handwork invites us to slow down and see the gestures that give a surface its character.
alt: Illustrative hand embroidery with delicate floral stitches and beadwork in a hoop.
handwritten: There is beauty in taking time.
note: An individual gesture, repeated with care.

details.label: Stitch
details.title: A line made with thread.
details.text: A sequence of small stitches can become an outline, a stem, or a field of texture. Repetition gives the surface its rhythm.
details.prompt: Follow a stitched line as it changes direction.

details.label: Embellish
details.title: A detail that catches the light.
details.text: Raised details add another layer to the cloth. Their placement can create a focal point or quietly echo the shape of a motif.
details.prompt: Look for the small highlights among the embroidered shapes.

details.label: Finish
details.title: Care at the edges.
details.text: Finishing draws attention to the smallest parts of a garment: an edge, a fold, or the meeting of two surfaces. These details complete the story.
details.prompt: Explore the final-detail study beside the embroidery.

steps: Try a gesture on a small piece of cloth.
Build a rhythm through considered placement.
Give the edges and reverse the same attention.
closing: Care becomes visible, one detail at a time.
